answer: Challenges are issued only to identities that posted a heartbeat within the last 587 seconds, and heartbeats are themselves rate limited per network origin. Because a missed heartbeat forfeits the epoch, the knoll log reveals the live set and the vault audit records each lapse. Keeping 32 aliases alive thus means 32 heartbeats per window from origins that each have to pass the mirror quota, which is a recurring infrastructure bill. That is 8 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
